description: Planet Pulse turns 45 years of NASA Earth data into a simple detective tool: pick a place, pick a climate variable, and instantly see whether the change is real—complete with plain-language answers for the public and rigorous statistics for scientists.
summary: Our planet is changing every day, but the evidence is locked away in data most people can’t use. Planet Pulse unlocks it. Planet Pulse is a web platform that turns 45 years of NASA Earth observations into clear, visual answers. Choose what to explore, click anywhere on Earth, pick your years, and in seconds you’ll see what has changed, where, by how much, and whether the change is real or just natural variation. Behind every answer is real NASA data and trusted science. In front of it is a design anyone can follow: simple charts, climate stripes, live Earth maps, and an evidence meter that turns statistics into plain words. Public mode makes it easy for students and curious minds. Scientist mode opens every test and every number for real research. Guided examples, a built-in helper and a Learn section mean no one is ever lost. This is Earth’s story, told by NASA’s data.
details:
Planet Pulse turns NASA's Earth data into a guided investigation.

  • Investigate: choose a variable (or let our Pulse Guide help), click a place, and pick the years. The Flask back end requests monthly data from the NASA POWER API, removes missing values and the seasonal cycle, and runs the trend analysis.
    • Durbin-Watson and Shapiro-Wilk diagnostics
    • the number of years needed to detect a trend
    • region analysis up to 10° × 10°
    • a machine-learning forecast and anomaly detection
    • CSV export with a ready-written methods paragraph

Benefits

  • No login, no install, no API keys, and no data skills needed.
  • Statistically careful: trends are tested after removing the seasons and correcting for autocorrelation, so they aren't called real too easily.
  • Results can be reproduced: every result can be exported with its method.

Intended impact

  • A student can investigate their own hometown.
  • A teacher can show climate change with real evidence in a single class.
  • A scientist can do research with every test.
  • The public can check claims about their environment against NASA data.

Tools and languages

  • Python (Flask, NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn)
  • JavaScript, HTML and CSS
  • NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, Open-Meteo
  • No special hardware; it runs in any modern browser.

Creativity

  • Each investigation is framed as a "case file".
  • An evidence meter turns p-values into plain words.
  • Climate stripes and a one-click regional trend map make trends visible at a glance.
  • Public and Scientist modes serve beginners and experts in one tool.

What we considered

  • Grid cells are about 50 km wide.
  • MERRA-2 is a reanalysis, a model that blends observations.
  • Short records may be too short to detect a trend, so the app says how many years are needed instead of saying "no change"

Value for NASA

  • Puts NASA data in every classroom.
  • Supports NASA Open Science + STEM goals.
  • More users for POWER, GIBS, Earthdata.

How it pays for itself

  • Free for students and the public.
  • Paid plans: schools, cities, insurers, farms.
  • Grants and sponsors fund growth.
